tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

134	| `INPUT_SURFACE` | Input Adapter (holds the one `SurfaceHandle` at MVP), the Interaction prompt object (no handle), Chart Table menu objects (no handle at MVP) | As `PRESENTATION` | As `PRESENTATION` | **May be issued a `SurfaceHandle` (ADR-0002); the class alone confers nothing.** Receives every tick's batch. 135	| `PROJECTOR` | Layout projector, `body.projector`, Lighting's occluder builder | As `PRESENTATION` | Engine-side *derived* objects its block owner's GDD names (nodes it creates, frees or reparents; tile and occluder content); declares the engine classes it may instantiate at registration | Never |
136	| `DIAGNOSTIC` | Debug Overlay (dev and playtest builds only; ADR-0031) | Everything, including kernel internals and `PERCEPTION_OUT`, through a separate diagnostics facet (`perception_access` true) | Its own overlay nodes only | Never |
137	| `REPLICATION` | Nobody at MVP (dormant until VS-B; ADR-0032) | n/a | n/a | n/a |
138

140	
141	**Read rules, each lint- or boot-checked:**
142	- Presentation reads simulation state only through `PresentationViews` and `PresentationClock`. It never holds `Kernel`, `SimViews`, `WriteScope`, `Command`, `BlockDescriptor` or a tick-phase context (`CallContext`, `ValidateContext`, `ApplyContext`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`). A lint forbids exactly those names in `src/presentation/` (ADR-0003 Risks already commits to it; the list is ADR-0010 ARCH-08's explicit deny list per TD-01). A handler legitimately names `ChangeBatch`, `NotifyContext` and `CompletionToken`, which are facet-side types (Key Interfaces).
143	- **`PERCEPTION_OUT` blocks are not subscribable or readable through a default `PresentationFacet`.** `perception_access` is `true` **only on the Perception Filter's facet and on `DIAGNOSTIC` facets, and `false` on every other facet** (the composition root sets it at issue; this ADR only declares which facets carry it). Enforcement is not ADR-0009's: (a) **subscribe time**, ADR-0004 subscribe-time check 6 (TD-08) refuses a subscription to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block from a facet without access with `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED`, which closes ADR-0004 OQ-7; (b) **read time**, ADR-0003 § 7 (amended by TD-07 item 10) gives `PresentationViews` two faces selected by the same flag: the default face returns the block's `empty_view` and counts `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`, the perception face returns the real facade. Lighting reads the Filter's per-viewer decoy list, an object the Filter owns, not the block. This follows `architecture.md` § API Boundaries ("Filter and Debug only") and Principle 3 over the broader wording in the kernel GDD's CR-10 table. ADR-0024 owns only the shape of the Filter's query surface.
144	- Presentation never reads another presenter's private state. A presenter may call a getter on a **strictly earlier stage's** product (the camera pose, the beam pose, the decoy list). Each presenter declares `reads: Array[int]` of stage ids at registration and the driver's freeze check fails boot if any entry is not strictly less than the presenter's own stage. A visual presenter never reads the Audio presenter or any audio level, bus meter, cue or voice state (TR-audio-042); Audio is stage 8 and nothing reads from it.
145	- The simulation (`src/kernel/`, `src/sim/`) never names a presentation class, a `Node`-derived class, `CanvasItem`, `Camera2D` or `Viewport`. `zoom`, `k`, `k_auto` and `field_h` appear only under `src/presentation/` and the Pipeline root (TR-shipbody-044); a lint checks the identifiers.
146	- Presentation reads settings (reduced motion, reduce flashing) from the settings store; **no simulation callable reads a setting**, and no toggle writes a block. A test runs one command stream with each toggle on and off and compares the tick count and `state_hash` (TR-pxl-034).
147	- **Cosmetic randomness: presentation hashes use `Ihash` or `Ihash.h32` (ADR-0005 § 2.6) with a fixed non-zero per-system seed**, never the global RNG, never `RandomNumberGenerator`, and **never `DetRng.derive` (ADR-0005 bans it in presentation)**. 150	
151	**The Layout PROJECTOR never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D`** (TR-section-024); Lighting's occluder builder is also a PROJECTOR and is the one class that does. 152

154	
155	### 2. Dirty-mark-then-draw
156	
157	**The handler contract.** The kernel invokes each subscriber handler through a registered `Callable` with a reused `NotifyContext` (ADR-0003 § 3), exactly like every other kernel-invoked callable. The shape is ADR-0003's, as fixed by ADR-0004 § 2 (re-read 2026-10-28; it matches):
158	
159	```gdscript
160	func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken:
161		_dirty.absorb(batch)        # ADR-0004 DirtyAccumulator (capacity facet.key_capacity); allocates nothing; is_all on overflow
162		return ctx.complete()       # last statement; nothing follows it
163	```
164	
165	This replaces the architecture document's `-> void` example (§ GDD sync). A handler **must** do only this: copy the batch's keys into the presenter's pre-sized dirty structure, copy the scalar fields it needs from an event record into a fixed-size ring, and return. A handler **must never**: read a view, touch a node, create a `Callable` or a container, emit an engine signal, `await`, call `submit`, or write any property. A handler returns its `CompletionToken` synchronously, so `await` is banned **lexically** in any script registered through a `PresenterDescriptor` or that calls `.subscribe(` (ADR-0010 PRES rule, TD-16, with a bad fixture); the kernel's token-identity check is the runtime backstop and records anything other than the armed token, including a suspended coroutine state, as `INCOMPLETE` (ADR-0004 § 2), which counts against the handler. 166	
167	**Why the handler does not draw.** It runs inside P5 with writes disabled and its cost is added to every other subscriber's; a catch-up frame already runs the tick loop up to four times (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`) and `INPUT_SURFACE` handlers run once per tick. 168	
169	**Delivery recap (properties this ADR relies on; ADR-0004 owns the mechanism):**
170	- PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches arrive **once per rendered frame**, after the frame's last tick, one `ChangeBatch` per dirty block per subscription, with the union of the frame's keys (`is_all` true past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256; this text's "`ALL`" means `batch.is_all`). INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick's batch. A 0-tick frame delivers nothing.
171	- A restore delivers one `is_all` batch per block to every class when `LOADING` becomes `RUNNING`, with `batch.tick` set to the restored `T` (ADR-0004 P5/load delivery). **`ChangeBatch` carries no load marker, by design** (ADR-0004 § 6 states it; see `PresentationClock.load_seq`), so `is_all` is indistinguishable from a mass change; the restore edge is `load_seq` (§ 6).
172	- Notifications carry no state; event records (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`) carry identifiers only.
173	
174	**The draw side.** Each presenter keeps two things, and its `present(frame)` early-outs only when both are empty:
175	- `dirty`: which blocks or keys changed since its last draw. Dirty drives **bulk and structural reads** (lists, queries, rebuilds, layout of plates): a presenter performs a bulk read of a block only when that block, or `ALL`, is dirty (TR-instr-005: derived inputs refresh once per Graph step because the Graph dirties its keys once per step, never per frame).
176	- `animating`: whether anything still moves on `tick_alpha` or `present_time` (an interpolated position, a needle ramp, a fade, flow scroll). **Interpolation needs a draw on frames with no notification**, because a 144 fps frame between two ticks has a new `tick_alpha` and no new state; the example in `architecture.md` that returns when `_dirty.is_empty()` would freeze motion on those frames and is corrected. Cheap scalar getters on the `interpolated` pair (previous and current position) may be read every frame while `animating`.
177	- `ALL` means "rebuild everything from the views, and draw the end state with no transition": the correct and sufficient response both to a restore and to a mass change. A presenter bounds a rebuild by its own budget (PROJECTOR: `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`, chunked across frames, continuing to draw the last complete state until the chunks finish).
178	- Event records are copied into a fixed ring; ring overflow degrades to a full rebuild and counts `PRESENTER_EVENT_OVERFLOW`. Events are never dropped silently, and a `BODY_TRANSFER` is delivered to the camera as a rebase, not a cut (TR-shipbody-049; the rebase math is ADR-0008's).
179	
180	**Coherence by construction.** The driver runs inside `PipelineRoot._process` at `PRESENTATION` (0), after the TickDriver (-50) in the same `_process` pass, and the kernel cannot tick while presentation runs, so every presenter in a frame reads the same committed tick `T`. No presenter copies state to be consistent.
181	
182	**Latency, stated honestly.** Discrete committed state (a bead appears, a light toggles) is drawn in the same rendered frame as the P5 that announced it, with zero frames of delay (TR-assembly-045). Continuously interpolated motion lags the commit by up to one tick by construction, because `tick_alpha` is clamped at 1 and never extrapolates (PR-4 rule 3, PR-9 rate table).

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

**Required sections:** Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences,
ADR Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed

**Status lifecycle:** `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`
- Never skip `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked
- Use `/architecture-decision` to create ADRs through the guided flow

**TR Registry:** `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
- Stable requirement IDs (e.g. `TR-movement-001`) that link GDD requirements to stories
- Never renumber existing IDs — only append new ones
- Updated by `/architecture-review` Phase 8

**Control Manifest:** `docs/architecture/control-manifest.md`
- Flat programmer rules sheet: Required / Forbidden / Guardrails per layer
- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header
- Stories embed this version; `/story-done` checks for staleness

**Validation:** Run `/architecture-review` after completing a set of ADRs.

## Engine Reference (`docs/engine-reference/`)

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

149	**Write allow-list (PRESENTATION and INPUT_SURFACE):** `CanvasItem` properties (including `position`, `visible`, `modulate`, `z_index`, `frame`, `flip_h`, `texture` and so on, with the placement rule of § 4), `Material` and shader parameters, `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D` and `CanvasModulate` properties, particle properties, and audio-player and audio-bus properties through the Audio presenter. Never: a block, a command (outside § 7), a physics body, `Camera2D.*`, `Viewport.*`, `SubViewport.*`, `SubViewportContainer.*` or `CanvasLayer.*` members **outside the Pipeline root and the camera host** (PR-8 item 4 and its lint AC), `Engine.time_scale`, `SceneTree.paused` (pause is the control plane's `PauseGate`, ADR-0002), synthetic input (`Input.parse_input_event`, `Input.action_press`), and file I/O (Settings and the Save host have their own owners).
150	
151	**The Layout PROJECTOR never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D`** (TR-section-024); Lighting's occluder builder is also a PROJECTOR and is the one class that does. The declared-classes list at registration is what the lint compares. The PROJECTOR scene shape, the Y-sort key and `entity_id` namespaces belong to ADR-0034 (this ADR owns placement only).
152	
153	A presenter output signal that crosses into simulation does not exist: the flow is state, notification, presentation, and never the reverse (CR-10 "Sim never calls presentation").
154	
155	### 2. Dirty-mark-then-draw
156	
157	**The handler contract.** The kernel invokes each subscriber handler through a registered `Callable` with a reused `NotifyContext` (ADR-0003 § 3), exactly like every other kernel-invoked callable. The shape is ADR-0003's, as fixed by ADR-0004 § 2 (re-read 2026-10-28; it matches):
158	
159	```gdscript
160	func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken:
161		_dirty.absorb(batch)        # ADR-0004 DirtyAccumulator (capacity facet.key_capacity); allocates nothing; is_all on overflow
162		return ctx.complete()       # last statement; nothing follows it
163	```
164	
165	This replaces the architecture document's `-> void` example (§ GDD sync). A handler **must** do only this: copy the batch's keys into the presenter's pre-sized dirty structure, copy the scalar fields it needs from an event record into a fixed-size ring, and return. A handler **must never**: read a view, touch a node, create a `Callable` or a container, emit an engine signal, `await`, call `submit`, or write any property. A handler returns its `CompletionToken` synchronously, so `await` is banned **lexically** in any script registered through a `PresenterDescriptor` or that calls `.subscribe(` (ADR-0010 PRES rule, TD-16, with a bad fixture); the kernel's token-identity check is the runtime backstop and records anything other than the armed token, including a suspended coroutine state, as `INCOMPLETE` (ADR-0004 § 2), which counts against the handler. A handler fault is counted and never fatal (ADR-0003).
166	
167	**Why the handler does not draw.** It runs inside P5 with writes disabled and its cost is added to every other subscriber's; a catch-up frame already runs the tick loop up to four times (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`) and `INPUT_SURFACE` handlers run once per tick. Reading views there would also read a state that a later tick in the same frame is about to replace.
168	
169	**Delivery recap (properties this ADR relies on; ADR-0004 owns the mechanism):**
170	- PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches arrive **once per rendered frame**, after the frame's last tick, one `ChangeBatch` per dirty block per subscription, with the union of the frame's keys (`is_all` true past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256; this text's "`ALL`" means `batch.is_all`). INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick's batch. A 0-tick frame delivers nothing.
171	- A restore delivers one `is_all` batch per block to every class when `LOADING` becomes `RUNNING`, with `batch.tick` set to the restored `T` (ADR-0004 P5/load delivery). **`ChangeBatch` carries no load marker, by design** (ADR-0004 § 6 states it; see `PresentationClock.load_seq`), so `is_all` is indistinguishable from a mass change; the restore edge is `load_seq` (§ 6).
172	- Notifications carry no state; event records (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`) carry identifiers only.
173	
174	**The draw side.** Each presenter keeps two things, and its `present(frame)` early-outs only when both are empty:
175	- `dirty`: which blocks or keys changed since its last draw. Dirty drives **bulk and structural reads** (lists, queries, rebuilds, layout of plates): a presenter performs a bulk read of a block only when that block, or `ALL`, is dirty (TR-instr-005: derived inputs refresh once per Graph step because the Graph dirties its keys once per step, never per frame).
176	- `animating`: whether anything still moves on `tick_alpha` or `present_time` (an interpolated position, a needle ramp, a fade, flow scroll). **Interpolation needs a draw on frames with no notification**, because a 144 fps frame between two ticks has a new `tick_alpha` and no new state; the example in `architecture.md` that returns when `_dirty.is_empty()` would freeze motion on those frames and is corrected. Cheap scalar getters on the `interpolated` pair (previous and current position) may be read every frame while `animating`.
177	- `ALL` means "rebuild everything from the views, and draw the end state with no transition": the correct and sufficient response both to a restore and to a mass change. A presenter bounds a rebuild by its own budget (PROJECTOR: `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`, chunked across frames, continuing to draw the last complete state until the chunks finish).
178	- Event records are copied into a fixed ring; ring overflow degrades to a full rebuild and counts `PRESENTER_EVENT_OVERFLOW`. Events are never dropped silently, and a `BODY_TRANSFER` is delivered to the camera as a rebase, not a cut (TR-shipbody-049; the rebase math is ADR-0008's).
179	
180	**Coherence by construction.** The driver runs inside `PipelineRoot._process` at `PRESENTATION` (0), after the TickDriver (-50) in the same `_process` pass, and the kernel cannot tick while presentation runs, so every presenter in a frame reads the same committed tick `T`. No presenter copies state to be consistent.
181	
182	**Latency, stated honestly.** Discrete committed state (a bead appears, a light toggles) is drawn in the same rendered frame as the P5 that announced it, with zero frames of delay (TR-assembly-045). Continuously interpolated motion lags the commit by up to one tick by construction, because `tick_alpha` is clamped at 1 and never extrapolates (PR-4 rule 3, PR-9 rate table).

186	### 3. One driver, one frame object, fixed named stages
187	
188	**`PipelineRoot` is the `PresentationHost`** (ruling TD-03; ADR-0008 owns the edit to its § 6.1, § 6.2 and § 7.3). It is one `Node` with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` and `process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, set from code, and it holds the `PresentationDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) that the composition root constructs and injects (ADR-0008 § 6.2). Its single `_process(delta)` does, in this order: (1) advance `present_time` (frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED`), (2) the zoom cooldown, (3) the `RESCALING` re-derive if dirty, (4) `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`. **No second node runs at `PRESENTATION` for presentation work**, so the priority-0 tie is removed by construction rather than by tree order, and `present_time` is current when the driver runs (this closes the host and ordering questions that earlier drafts left to ADR-0008). **Presenters define no `_process`.** They register a `PresenterDescriptor` with the driver in `BOOTING`; the driver freezes the registry with the kernel and sorts it once by stage.
189	
190	This is the "explicit driver" the HUD GDD asks for (OQ-HS-44, OQ-HS-51, ADR candidate F). It replaces N nodes whose relative order would depend on priority sub-constants and tree order with one loop over a fixed-size array, which is testable headless with stub presenters (AC-HS-89) and does not depend on the cross-node `process_priority` result for any presenter. The PROJECTOR scene shape, the Y-sort key and `entity_id` namespaces belong to ADR-0034 (this ADR owns placement only).

**Lighting's occluder builder is chunk-exempt inside a shadow light's reach (amended 2026-10-29, sync knock-on fix, round 3; 2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md LO-11).** The builder rebuilds a section that intersects an active shadow light's reach disc as a **single chunk, exempt from the `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` slice**, and applies the resulting polygons to its pooled `LightOccluder2D` nodes in **one apply at the end of its last chunk**. Stage 0 (`PROJECT`) therefore completes that apply before the `LIGHTING` stage (6) of the same frame, so a lit frame never draws a half-updated occluder set ("light through a wall" cannot appear for an in-reach section). **Any other rebuild** (a section outside every active shadow light's reach, or an `ALL` rebuild across many sections) stays chunked: the old complete occluder set keeps drawing, nothing is applied piecemeal, and the frames until the final apply are counted as event frames (Lighting's LO-11 counter), not as a ceiling breach. The exemption belongs to the occluder builder only; the Layout projector and `body.projector` keep the `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME` slice.
